req:a-local-client-works-against-a-remote-reflow2-server-by-url, point 2: "On a stateless server the only way to say it is per request, so the client carries `_meta[\"reflow2/writes_for\"]` on every call it forwards ... A shared credential says which client, never which person."

WHY IT HAS NOT BITTEN YET, as far as is known: on flo2.io each person signs in with their own credential, and the gateway binds the writer from it (flo2's fact:root-cause-the-door-rebinds-approver-and-says-so-only-in-its-refusal-2026-09-28). The gap shows on an organisation's shared server reached with ONE shared key, the case point 2 was written for. There, every write would be credited to whoever the key names, or to nobody.

WHERE IT STANDS IN THE PLAN: the requirement is SCHEDULED_FOR position 7's epoch as a whole, but the epoch's text says it "delivers point 3". No other planned step names point 2.
